bibl.title: A pneumonia outbreak associated with a new coronavirus of probable bat origin

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: a virus with no name yet - identified, sequenced, classified and provisionally named in one paper, and RENAMED BY A COMMITTEE BEFORE THE PAPER WAS PRINTED
span.quote: Following the name given by the World Health Organization (WHO), we tentatively call it novel coronavirus 2019 (2019-nCoV).

span.label: what the Wuhan pneumonia outbreak was caused by, where it sits taxonomically, and whether it uses the SARS-CoV receptor
span.quote: The sequences are almost identical and share 79.6% sequence identity to SARS-CoV. Furthermore, we show that 2019-nCoV is 96% identical at the whole-genome level to a bat coronavirus.

span.label: five full-length genomes from early patients, the 96.2% match to a bat coronavirus, the species assignment, and the confirmation that the virus enters cells through ACE2
span.quote: Notably, we confirmed that 2019-nCoV uses the same cell entry receptor—angiotensin converting enzyme II (ACE2)—as SARS-CoV.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Of the 10,038,758 total reads—of which 1,582 total reads were retained after filtering of reads from the human genome—1,378 (87.1%) sequences matched the sequence of SARSr-CoV

span.label: an outbreak whose cause was defined CLINICALLY before anything was sequenced - by symptoms, blood counts, radiography, and a failure to improve on antibiotics
span.quote: The disease was determined to be caused by virus-induced pneumonia by clinicians according to clinical symptoms and other criteria, including a rise in body temperature, decreases in the number of lymphocytes and white blood cells (although levels of the latter were sometimes normal), new pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiography and no obvious improvement after treatment with antibiotics for three days.

span.label: pan-CoV PCR on samples from seven ICU patients, then metagenomic next-generation sequencing of one bronchoalveolar lavage sample, de novo assembly, targeted PCR, and phylogenetic analysis against known SARSr-CoVs
span.term: pan-CoV PCR on samples from seven ICU patients, then metagenomic next-generation sequencing of one bronchoalveolar lavage sample, de novo assembly, targeted PCR, and phylogenetic analysis against known SARSr-CoVs
span.quote: Of the 10,038,758 total reads—of which 1,582 total reads were retained after filtering of reads from the human genome—1,378 (87.1%) sequences matched the sequence of SARSr-CoV

span.label: THE IDENTIFICATION SURVIVES A FILTER THAT REMOVES 99.98% OF THE DATA: `of the 10,038,758 total reads - of which 1,582 TOTAL READS WERE RETAINED after filtering of reads from the human genome - 1,378 (87.1%) sequences matched`. THE 87.1% IS A PERCENTAGE OF THE SURVIVORS, and the finding rests on 1,378 reads out of ten million
span.quote: Of the 10,038,758 total reads—of which 1,582 total reads were retained after filtering of reads from the human genome—1,378 (87.1%) sequences matched the sequence of SARSr-CoV

span.label: and the taxonomic placement is a threshold on a CHOSEN SUBSTRING: whole-genome identity to SARS-CoV is 79.6%, but `the seven conserved replicase domains in ORF1ab THAT WERE USED FOR CoV SPECIES CLASSIFICATION were 94.4% identical`. Same species by one measure and twenty per cent apart by another
span.quote: However, the amino acid sequences of the seven conserved replicase domains in ORF1ab that were used for CoV species classification were 94.4% identical between 2019-nCoV and SARS-CoV, suggesting that the two viruses belong to the same species, SARSr-CoV.

span.label: THE NAME IN THE BODY IS ALREADY OBSOLETE AND THE PAPER SAYS SO IN A NOTE: `Note added in proof: since this paper was accepted, THE ICTV HAS DESIGNATED THE VIRUS AS SARS-CoV-2; in addition, the WHO has released THE OFFICIAL NAME OF THE DISEASE ... COVID-19`. The record carries both names AND the moment of the change
span.quote: Note added in proof: Since this paper was accepted, the ICTV has designated the virus as SARS-CoV-2 15 ; in addition, the WHO has released the official name of the disease caused by this virus, which is COVID-19

span.label: and the name it does use was provisional and institutional from the start: `FOLLOWING THE NAME GIVEN BY THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION (WHO), WE TENTATIVELY CALL IT novel coronavirus 2019`. Neither name in this paper is the authors' own
span.quote: Following the name given by the World Health Organization (WHO), we tentatively call it novel coronavirus 2019 (2019-nCoV).

span.label: THE SPECIES BOUNDARY IS A CONVENTION ABOUT WHICH SEQUENCE TO COMPARE, and the paper states the convention in the same clause it applies it - `that were used for CoV species classification`. A different choice of region gives a different answer, and 79.6% is in the same abstract as 94.4%
span.quote: However, the amino acid sequences of the seven conserved replicase domains in ORF1ab that were used for CoV species classification were 94.4% identical between 2019-nCoV and SARS-CoV, suggesting that the two viruses belong to the same species, SARSr-CoV.

span.label: the design is declared to have no statistical structure at all: `NO STATISTICAL METHODS WERE USED TO PREDETERMINE SAMPLE SIZE. The experiments were NOT RANDOMIZED and the investigators were NOT BLINDED`. Five genomes from five patients in an unfolding outbreak
span.quote: No statistical methods were used to predetermine sample size. The experiments were not randomized and the investigators were not blinded to allocation during experiments and outcome assessment.

span.label: and the sequence difference that matters most functionally is left open: whether the three N-terminal insertions in the S protein `confer sialic-acid-binding activity as it does in MERS-CoV NEEDS TO BE FURTHER STUDIED`
span.quote: Whether the insertions in the N-terminal domain of the S protein of 2019-nCoV confer sialic-acid-binding activity as it does in MERS-CoV needs to be further studied.

span.label: five independent full-length genomes from five different patients
span.note: eliminates: a single-sample artefact - the four later sequences were `MORE THAN 99.9% IDENTICAL to each other`, and the identification does not rest on one library · outcome: held
span.quote: The sequences are almost identical and share 79.6% sequence identity to SARS-CoV. Furthermore, we show that 2019-nCoV is 96% identical at the whole-genome level to a bat coronavirus.

span.label: the species assignment was made on the region conventionally used for it, not on the whole genome
span.note: eliminates: nothing about the boundary itself - it applies a convention rather than testing one, and the paper reports both figures (79.6% whole-genome, 94.4% replicase) in the same abstract · outcome: partial
span.quote: However, the amino acid sequences of the seven conserved replicase domains in ORF1ab that were used for CoV species classification were 94.4% identical between 2019-nCoV and SARS-CoV, suggesting that the two viruses belong to the same species, SARSr-CoV.

span.label: the design's statistical structure
span.note: eliminates: nothing, declared: `NO STATISTICAL METHODS WERE USED TO PREDETERMINE SAMPLE SIZE. The experiments were not randomized and the investigators were not blinded` · outcome: failed
span.quote: No statistical methods were used to predetermine sample size. The experiments were not randomized and the investigators were not blinded to allocation during experiments and outcome assessment.

span.label: `2019-nCoV` - THE NAME THIS PAPER USES THROUGHOUT, AND IT WAS DEAD BEFORE PUBLICATION. `Following the name given by the WHO, we TENTATIVELY call it ...`, and then the note in proof: `the ICTV HAS DESIGNATED the virus as SARS-CoV-2`. The record's own subject terms say SARS-CoV-2 while its text says 2019-nCoV
span.quote: Note added in proof: Since this paper was accepted, the ICTV has designated the virus as SARS-CoV-2 15 ; in addition, the WHO has released the official name of the disease caused by this virus, which is COVID-19

span.label: `the same species` - AS OPERATIONALISED HERE, 94.4% amino-acid identity across SEVEN CONSERVED REPLICASE DOMAINS, `THAT WERE USED FOR CoV SPECIES CLASSIFICATION`. The whole-genome figure in the same abstract is 79.6%. THE SPECIES IS A PROPERTY OF THE REGION YOU ALIGN
span.quote: However, the amino acid sequences of the seven conserved replicase domains in ORF1ab that were used for CoV species classification were 94.4% identical between 2019-nCoV and SARS-CoV, suggesting that the two viruses belong to the same species, SARSr-CoV.

span.label: `87.1%` - a percentage of 1,582 reads, which are what remained of 10,038,758 after human sequence was filtered out. The denominator of the headline proportion is the SURVIVORS OF A FILTER, not the sample
span.quote: Of the 10,038,758 total reads—of which 1,582 total reads were retained after filtering of reads from the human genome—1,378 (87.1%) sequences matched the sequence of SARSr-CoV

span.label: the disease, BEFORE ANY VIRUS: defined by `clinical symptoms and other criteria, including a rise in body temperature, decreases in the number of lymphocytes and white blood cells ..., new pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiography and NO OBVIOUS IMPROVEMENT AFTER TREATMENT WITH ANTIBIOTICS FOR THREE DAYS`. A definition partly by failure of a treatment
span.quote: The disease was determined to be caused by virus-induced pneumonia by clinicians according to clinical symptoms and other criteria, including a rise in body temperature, decreases in the number of lymphocytes and white blood cells (although levels of the latter were sometimes normal), new pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiography and no obvious improvement after treatment with antibiotics for three days.
